invariants.note: Single SWAP kernel unaffected; aggregation lives in runtime/coupler composition.
No file, format, path, parsing or file-unit dependency introduced.
Tile fractions and exchange inputs remain separate from physical column state.
No new persistent SWAP-column physical state introduced.
No solver scratch moved into persistent column state.
Flat tile arrays remain compatible with batching, SoA and parallel aggregation.
Aggregation is side-effect free and does not publish rejected physical trials.
No trial warm-start semantics are changed.
No calendar unit or day boundary enters the aggregation primitive.
Aggregation accepts any admitted coupling-window exchange quantity.
Groundwater cell composition is explicit runtime functionality.
Groundwater exchange sign remains exact opposite of aggregated SWAP exchange.
Area weighting conserves the exchange quantity; no mass tolerance or correction is introduced.
Interface-sensitivity production remains independent and unmodified.
Aggregation adds no extra SWAP trajectories.
Primitive supports many tiles and many cells without per-tile solver instances.
Multiple surface tiles per groundwater cell are explicitly supported; fractions must close and are never silently normalized.
Non-SWAP/deep-vadose tile ownership can remain external; no forced full-physics tile is created.
Aggregation neither creates nor removes component storage.
Soil-water solver choice is irrelevant to this runtime primitive.
No SWAP process physics is duplicated in the aggregation layer.
No dependency on HeadCalc internals introduced.
Tile composition is not encoded as a physical solver option.
No retry or fallback path is added.
Reference mode remains unchanged.
Invalid fractions/mappings fail closed and are directly diagnosable.
Aggregation cost exists only for composed groundwater tiles.
Tile-to-cell mapping and area fractions are explicitly runtime/coupler-owned.
No silent MODFLOW, file-format, calendar or 1:1 mapping assumption is introduced.
Change explicitly audited against all architecture invariants.
